## Requirements (from spec)
- R1 Event writer: transactional append; seq assignment; whitelist validation at write boundary (REQ-DATA-37).
- R2 Storage: `run_events` daily partitions (visibility=user, project lifetime); `run_events_internal` 30-day retention.
- R3 Ingest robustness: batch ≤250 or 2s; disk buffering when api unreachable; >5000 buffered → engine pause; drop nothing.
- R4 Fan-out+SSE: Redis PUBLISH run:<id> {seq}; GET /runs/:id/events?after=seq SSE; replay rows>after (user only) then tail; `:ping` 25s; p95≤2s no buffering; viewers Summary density only (REQ-DATA-38).

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1 SSE reconnect Last-Event-ID replays exactly-once (dup/gap across forced disconnect).
- AC2 internal-type leak test: no internal row ever served on SSE (REQ-ARCH-12).
- AC3 Redis outage: tail degrades, replay-from-PG still serves; Redis never source of truth.
- AC4 Ingest under unreachable-api: events buffer to disk, land in order; >5000 raises pause signal.
- AC5 Partition/retention: internal rows expire at 30 days; user rows survive.
- AC6 Payload violating P0.02 schema (or >280-char free text) rejected at write boundary (REQ-DATA-37).

## Cross-cutting invariants
- Events never carry prompt/reasoning/private-memory/raw page text (REQ-DATA-37).
- UI never infers state from events alone; transitions pair with events transactionally (REQ-DATA-33).

## Design decisions
- One shared per-run seq space (gap-free) via `run_event_seq` upsert `returning`. User rows → partitioned `run_events`; internal → `run_events_internal`. Seq gaps in run_events (from internal) are fine for `seq>after` replay.
- Redis = wakeup only, carries high-water seq; the SSE tail always reads actual rows from Postgres (source of truth). Publish best-effort inside the writer; streamer has a safety re-poll so a lost/early wakeup self-heals; reconnect (Last-Event-ID) always replays from PG.
- RLS: `run_events` (served to viewers) + `run_event_seq` under FORCE RLS (tenant = current_tenant()). `run_events_internal` NOT under RLS (like access_log/fetch_log) so the system-scoped retention delete works; it is never served to viewers (structural AC2 guarantee: SSE reads only run_events, which holds only user rows).
- Partitioning: parent PARTITION BY RANGE(day) + DEFAULT partition (drop-nothing safety net); `ensureRunEventsPartition` + worker job pre-creates daily partitions. Internal retention by DELETE where at<now-30d.
- Density: viewers get Summary only; run requester gets up to verbose. `readUserEventsAfter(maxDensity)` filters.
